#1834. Fiorentina vs Juventus - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 06 Nov 2026 09:07

Sending Serie A into the international break, old foes Fiorentina and Juventus will clash at Stadio Franchi on Sunday night.

While the Viola are still seeking their first home win of the season, fallen giants Juve have been left trailing Italy's top six.

In contrast to their domestic woes, Juventus have lost just one of their last 11 UEFA fixtures - scoring at least twice in nine - and their latest success arrived on Thursday evening.

Though they had to survive a late siege away to AZ Alkmaar, the Bianconeri secured a third win from four Europa League games thanks to goals from Randal Kolo Muani and Teun Koopmeiners, who inevitably scored against his old club.

That 2-1 victory leaves them well set to reach the knockout stage without needing a playoff, as they sit fifth midway through this season's league phase.

However, they have only taken 17 points from their first 10 Serie A matches, putting pressure on Luciano Spalletti, who recently completed his first year in charge.

Soon after losing 2-0 to Genoa, Juve faced his former club Napoli last weekend, when stunning strikes from Kerim Alajbegovic and Jeremie Boga eventually secured an unconvincing victory in Turin.

Occupying seventh place, Spalletti's injury-hit squad still lie 11 points behind surprise league leaders Lazio, and they also trail newly promoted Frosinone.

Now, having lost two of their last four top-flight away games, Juventus must head to the Franchi, where they have only won once across their last seven visits.

After losing three on the spin without scoring, Fiorentina are currently unbeaten in four games against Juventus, including a memorable 3-0 home triumph in March 2025.

There is no love lost between the pair, whose rivalry reached new levels when Roberto Baggio swapped Florence for Turin back in 1990, and several others have since trod the same path.

Ahead of this week's clash, Fiorentina seem to have turned a corner, claiming four points from their last two outings - a home draw with Atalanta, and Monday's away victory over Sassuolo.

Trailing 1-0 with half time approaching, the Viola's forwards finally clicked into gear, with Mateo Pellegrino, Alieu Njie and Franco Mastantuono all finding the net in an eventful 4-2 win.

Yet, Fiorentina are sitting 16th in the table on a modest eight points, having already recalled former interim coach Paolo Vanoli following another terrible start to the campaign.

After beginning with a seven-game winless streak there last season, they have struggled at Stadio Franchi again: the Tuscan club have picked up just two points from their first five home matches.

Three days on from a successful trip to the Netherlands, Juventus boss Spalletti may be keen to rotate his squad, but several men are still missing as Juve's injury crisis continues.

Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Francisco Conceicao, Kamil Grabara, Zeki Celik, Nico Gonzalez and captain Manuel Locatelli are all in the treatment room, while Weston McKennie's presence is in some doubt.

Though summer signing Jeff Ekhator has just returned, Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade will hope to start and convert their continental form into domestic goals: the pair have five strikes between them from four Europa League matches, but they have contributed just one in Serie A.

By contrast, Real Madrid loanee Mastantuono now has four league goals for Fiorentina, and he should link up with Pellegrino and Njie in the final third.

The hosts must make do without injured trio Fabiano Parisi, Arthur Atta and Marin Pongracic, while Luca Ranieri's foot problem will be assessed ahead of the game.

Should Ranieri miss out, Vanoli would only have two senior centre-backs available: versatile Brazilian defender Viery and ex-Juve man Radu Dragusin.

De Gea; Jimenez, Dragusin, Viery, Mario; Ndour, Fagioli, Oulai; Mastantuono, Pellegrino, Njie

Vicario; Kalulu, Bremer, Lucumi, Cabal; Sarr, Luiz, Koopmeiners; Kolo Muani, Alajbegovic; Woltemade

Both teams have been too inconsistent to match their pre-season aims, making the outcome on Sunday night quite tough to predict.

Juve are assured of a hostile reception in Florence, but the hosts tend to wilt in front of their own fans - so, all three points will go back to Turin.

#1833. Carrick says Man Utd must ‘live in the present’ amid Ferguson comparisons

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Michael Carrick says Manchester United must "live in the present" amid comparisons between his struggles in the Old Trafford hot seat and those endured by Alex Ferguson in the early stages of his tenure.

Carrick got some much-needed respite on Tuesday as United fought back from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League, halting a nine-game winless run (D3 L6).

But Ipswich Town are the only side the Red Devils have beaten in nine Premier League matches this campaign (D4 L4).

They have not started a league season with as few as one win in their first 10 games since 1972-73, while only three teams in English top-flight history have made such a start to a campaign after finishing in the top three in the previous season – Derby County in 1894-95, Chelsea in 1920-21, and Arsenal in 1953-54.

United sit 17th in the table ahead of Sunday's meeting with Aston Villa, and depending on results elsewhere, they could be in the relegation zone by the time that game begins.

United have not been in the drop zone at least nine matches into a season since November 1986, at the start of Ferguson's illustrious 27-year reign, which ultimately contained 38 trophy wins including 13 Premier League titles and two Champions League triumphs.

But when Carrick was asked if the United hierarchy needed to show him the same faith as his former mentor received, he pushed back on the suggestion.

"The game has certainly changed, no doubt. It has evolved. It changes, and we have got to deal with what is in front of us," he told reporters on Friday.

"The comparison, I get, and I understand. We have got to live in the present. We're all desperate to win football matches and win them as quickly as we can.

"You always find something to compare us to! It is up to us to take it forward. It [the win over Roma] was a fantastic night, but it was a one-off night.

"Nothing is done yet. Nothing has been achieved yet. It is one moment in time that we need to use to move forward. We need more of it, for sure."

A legend among legends. Today marks the 40 years since Sir Alex Ferguson began his glorious association with Manchester United  https://t.co/E6anjZtHQu

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 6, 2026

United are winless in their last seven Premier League games (D4 L3), only enduring a longer run without a victory in the competition in April and May 2025 (eight matches), which was ended by a 2-0 home win over Villa.

But Carrick insists he has seen positive signs from his side, even if individual errors came into play during the first half of the Roma game.

"When you watch the [Roma] game back in the first half, it wasn't so bad," Carrick said. "There were moments where we left ourselves short – they're the moments we have got to clean up.

"There are little moments here and there that have changed games for us, which is football and something we have to manage – the first half against Chelsea was very good.

"I think we are showing signs of improvement in that respect. We have got to take that moving forward."

#1832. Arsenal: Mikel Arteta sends France clear William Saliba message before squad selection

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta insists that Arsenal would have no issue with William Saliba being called up to the France squad.

Saliba has not played a single minute of football for either club or country so far this season, having been on the sidelines with a back injury since he was forced off in the World Cup semi-final defeat by Spain in July.

The centre-back has stepped up his recovery in recent weeks and on Wednesday made his first return to Arsenal’s matchday squad.

Saliba was an unused substitute against Slavia Prague in the Champions League and it remains to be seen whether he is involved against Hull in the Premier League on Saturday.

There is a chance that Saliba’s first minutes this season come with France rather than Arsenal, with the defender in contention to be named in Zinedine Zidane’s latest Les Bleus squad.

Arsenal have been in discussions with the French medical staff over Saliba’s situation.

“We’ve been in very close contact,” Arteta said on Friday. “They’re announcing [their squad] at 5pm this evening.

“They have all the information, now it’s about them, about Zinedine in this case to make the call. We will accept whatever it is.”

Arteta also suggested that Saliba joining up with France could be a positive for Arsenal, as the club look to build his fitness.

France travel to take on Italy next Thursday before hosting Turkey three days later in their final Nations League matches.

Asked whether he had concerns about Saliba being named in the French squad, Arteta said: “It’s something that is between them more.

“William needs minutes as well. I know how much he loves it, to be in and around the national team.

“It’s a new manager [Zidane], a really exciting one as well. Whatever is decided, it’s fine for us.”

#1831. Tottenham: Roberto De Zerbi considered surprise Luca Williams-Barnett role for rare Chelsea win

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed he thought about starting teenage sensation Luca Williams-Barnett ahead of Tottenham’s historic victory at Chelsea last month.

Williams-Barnett has been the name on everyone’s lips since his scintillating Premier League debut against Crystal Palace last weekend, nearly grabbing an assist with a superb run and cross for Mohammed Kudus.

The 18-year-old has, however, had to watch as his England contemporaries Rio Mgumoha and Max Dowman have been given ample opportunities to impress, with De Zerbi admitting he had been reluctant to risk him while Spurs struggled for results.

Spurs were winless after the first six league games of this season, but have begun to pick up results in the last few weeks and are looking to make it four wins in a row for the first time in more than 1,000 days when they travel to Leeds in the early kick-off on Saturday afternoon.

De Zerbi feels he has a responsibility to look after Williams-Barnett, who he has previously said has the right blend of arrogance and confidence to be a top player, and admits he thought better of throwing him in against Chelsea, even though he believed he was ready to start the game.

“To find the time is my responsibility because when you manage such young players, with such a big talent like Luca, it is a bigger responsibility for me, and he has to be ready when he goes on the pitch,” De Zerbi said in his pre-Leeds press conference on Friday afternoon.

“I think it (does) not depend on the result, he can play at the beginning. Before the Chelsea game, I thought to play with him in the first XI but at the end you have to find the right moment for them also.”

Williams-Barnett, shortlisted for October’s Creative Moment of the Month by the Premier League for his dazzling bit of skill against Palace, has long been thought of as one of the most exciting talents to come out of Spurs’ academy since Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

His minutes, though, have been limited to two substitute appearances and a total of 14 minutes this season despite his promotion to the first-team.

De Zerbi is aware of Williams-Barnett’s potential, acknowledging that he knew he had a special player on his hands as early as pre-season, and with Spurs finding form, he now feels more open to using him more frequently.

#1830. Man United transfer news: JJ Gabriel set to agree deal with future club, compensation revealed

By Axel Clody | 06 Nov 2026 09:08, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 10:44

JJ Gabriel has chosen his future club and has just agreed a deal with it. The compensation Manchester United will receive for the move has also been revealed.

The suspense is over in the JJ Gabriel saga. Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and Barcelona were named as suitors for the 16-year-old gem, after the attacking midfielder indicated that he wished to leave Manchester United at the start of the new campaign.

The three reasons for the split have been revealed: his use during pre-season was insufficient, he feels he should have been involved in the Champions League match against Sabah, and the Red Devils did not offer him a direct enough path to the first team.

Following that revelation, a battle between European heavyweights raged for several weeks. Real Madrid are now set to win it.

The Spanish giants are on the verge of completing the signing of the Manchester United gem, according to Florian Plettenberg.

A verbal agreement has already been reached. The transfer is scheduled for 1 January 2027, thanks to JJ Gabriel’s European passport. Manchester United will receive only training compensation, amounting to £306,000 (€360,000). That is a small sum for a 16-year-old prodigy courted by Europe’s giants.

Marca adds that the England Under-17 international should first join Castilla, under the supervision of Jose Mourinho and his staff. His performances will then dictate whether he is ready to play in Real Madrid’s senior squad.

#1829. Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso reacts to Cole Palmer latest England squad snub: 'We have not spoken'

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has said he has not spoken to Cole Palmer about his latest omission from the England squad.

On Friday morning, it was announced that Palmer had not been called up by Thomas Tuchel for the Three Lions' Nations League games against Croatia and Spain next week.

This came after England had made medical checks over the attacking midfielder, who was initially selected in the England squad for the autumn international break but dropped out with a minor injury.

It means Palmer has not played for England since the March camp as he was also left out of Tuchel’s World Cup squad in the summer.

Alonso was asked at his press conference on Friday afternoon whether he had spoken to Palmer about the most recent snub and said: “No, we have not spoken about that.

“We are very happy with Cole. He is connecting very well with the other attackers and is helping the team.”

Tuchel has since repeated his belief that the Chelsea star “misses too many opportunities to impress” for his country.

“Everyone is desperate to play for England, and Cole is no exception," The England boss said.

“But, again, what I said last time: he misses too many opportunities to impress. Two-and-a-half weeks was a long time [to miss]. The door is always open, but nothing has changed, and we decided [to go] without him.”

Alonso, meanwhile, also added that he wouldn't tell players to miss the international break.

"No. I never tell," the Spaniard said. "When a player is fully fit, he's selectable. When he's not fit, we try to give the national team reasonable information to decide together.

“Sometimes it's not good for the player."

Paulo Fonseca is leaving Lyon and it could have a knock-on effect for AC Milan in the winter mercato, it seems.

With Athekame’s rise at Lyon, there are several people to thank. However, Fonseca deserves substantial praise for getting the most out of the young Swiss defender. Indeed, he always showed signs of promise and now, it’s tangible.

The Portuguese gave him a starting role in his defence, and he hasn’t looked back, playing Athekame nine times in Ligue 1 this season. However, things could change now.

According to MilanNews, Fonseca’s departure – headed to Sporting – could ‘alter the balance’ at the Groupama Stadium and offer an opportunity for the Rossoneri to recall their player. After all, he was heavily against his departure in mid-season.

For Athekame, the prospect of working under a new coach may not be as rewarding, too. So, he may also prefer a return to the Diavolo, where a role is ready for him on the right of Ruben Amorim’s back four.

There is no recall clause in the deal, so it won’t be easy and will likely require some financial outlay. Nevertheless, Fonseca may have helped Milan here, even if it’s only indirectly. More about his situation should be learned over the next few weeks.

#1827. Bayern aiming to take momentum from Madrid to Mainz, says Danks

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Aaron Danks is hoping Bayern Munich's win over Atletico Madrid can be used as momentum ahead of this weekend's trip to Mainz, going into the November international break.

Following back-to-back draws with Viking and Arsenal in Europe, Bayern returned to winning ways with a 2-0 triumph at the Estadio Metropolitano on Tuesday.

Both goals came in the second half, with Lennart Karl's opener followed up by Konrad Laimer's thumping 74th-minute finish as Bayern capitalised on some poor Atletico defending.

After also beating Real Madrid 2-1 away in last season's quarter-finals, Bayern have won consecutive away games in Spain in major European competitions for the first time ever.

Bayern (51) became the second top-five European league side to hit 50 goals in all competitions this season after Barcelona (60), and with the defending Bundesliga champions level on points with Borussia Dortmund at the summit, Danks acknowledged the importance of their confidence-boosting result.

"We've analysed it. The most important thing is that the team spirit, the approach of the players, never giving up, fighting to the end is there. We'll take that with us," he said.

"We'll try out a few things. There's a lot of rotation, a lot of movement, and the full-backs are involved in the attack.

"We've got plenty of players available there, which gives us options, as does our strong midfield. We'll play as normal, in our usual style, finding solutions with different players.

"Who those players are, we'll discuss that amongst the coaching staff. We'll try a few things out and then see how it goes."

𝗔𝗮𝗿𝗼𝗻 𝗗𝗮𝗻𝗸𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗠𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘇 𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘄 “We’ve always had tough matches against Mainz. Last year we were 3-0 down. We respect them. It’s a difficult place to play. — FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 6, 2026

Bayern will be looking to end a positive week both on and off the field on an even bigger high, after Harry Kane pledged his future to the club earlier this week.

Kane, who recently became the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since 2001, has put pen to paper on a new contract with Bayern, keeping him in Germany until 2029.

Since joining from Tottenham in 2023, Kane has netted 156 times in just 161 appearances in all competitions and is already sixth in Bayern's all-time scoring charts, only behind Gerd Muller (565), Robert Lewandowski (344), Thomas Muller (250), Rainer Ohlhauser (229) and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (217).

His Ballon d'Or triumph was the first by a Bayern player since Rummenigge in 1981, and the first by any Bundesliga player since Borussia Dortmund's Matthias Sammer in 1996.

"We're really happy that the best player in the world right now has committed to Bayern," Danks said of Kane. "He feels really good here. You can also sense that.

"It's important to have a figure like him here. He's exceeded all expectations from experts. We firmly believe he can maintain his level with his attitude and personality and help us.

"If we didn't believe that, we wouldn't have extended. The truth is on the pitch. I believe he'll continue to show that in the coming years."

Mainz, meanwhile, come into the game off the back of three consecutive defeats in all competitions, the latest of which saw them trounced 4-1 by Elversberg.

They will be without the suspended Stefan Posch and Phillipp Mwene for the visit of Bayern, too.

Posch has averaged the most passes per 90 minutes for Mainz in the Bundesliga this season (60) and has missed only one start for the club since his debut in January this year (a 0-0 draw against Paderborn on MD1).

If Mainz are to get anything out of this game, they will need Becker to be on top of his game.

Becker leads Mainz in the Bundesliga for goal contributions (six – two goals, four assists), while his 18 chances created are only bettered by Nadiem Amiri (27).

Kane has already provided six assists in the Bundesliga this season, surpassing his total from the whole of last term (five in 31 games).

Only Werder Bremen's Marco Grull has more assists in the league (seven).

However, the Ballon d'Or holder has failed to score in each of his last two Bundesliga appearances – he has only had a longer goal drought once in the competition (five games between February and March 2025).

Generational footballer. https://t.co/ELN2OFkXqe

— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) November 5, 2026

Bayern came from 3-0 down to win 4-3 on their last Bundesliga trip to Mainz, in April this year – that was one of only three matches in the club's Bundesliga history where they have overturned a three-goal deficit to win.

The Bundesliga champions are also unbeaten in their last 30 top-flight away games (W22 D8) – only once have they had a longer unbeaten run on the road, a 33-game streak between 2012 and 2014. Their last away defeat in the competition came against their upcoming opponents Mainz in December 2024 (1-2).

However, Bayern have 18 points after eight matches, their worst start to a Bundesliga season in four years; they had only 15 points at this stage in 2022-23. Last season, they started with a maximum of 24 points from their opening eight games.

Mainz, meanwhile, have lost two consecutive Bundesliga games for the first time under Urs Fischer and are winless in their last seven Bundesliga home matches (D1 L6), the longest ongoing run in the division.

Indeed, Mainz have picked up just one point at home this season (D1 L3), the joint-fewest in the league alongside last-placed Borussia Monchengladbach.

They have also conceded 17 goals in their last six Bundesliga matchdays – more than any other club in that period, having kept a clean sheet in their first two games of the season. Mainz have conceded the most goals in the opening 15 minutes (six) and the most in the first half (10) of any team in the league this season.

#1826. Mikel Arteta reveals reaction to Noni Madueke's England snub as Arsenal get boost

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has backed Arsenal winger Noni Madueke to recover quickly from his latest England disappointment.

Madueke was not named in Thomas Tuchel’s Three Lions squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain.

That is despite the 24-year-old putting together the best run of form in his Arsenal career so far, stepping up in the absence of the injured Bukayo Saka.

Madueke has four goal involvements in his last eight matches and sent Arsenal on their way to victory over Slavia Prague in the Champions League in midweek by opening the scoring.

It has been a timely run, with Saka out with a quad injury, and it came after Madueke was also omitted from the England squad for the last international window in September.

Arteta revealed at the time that Madueke had been the best player in training after that setback, and the Arsenal boss was again full of praise on Friday as he expanded on how the winger has cemented his place in the Gunners’ side.

“What he did was go abroad and he trained,” Arteta said. “He got somebody to train and he wanted a programme. He wanted to do that. That’s Noni and that’s his mindset. He wants to get better.

“I love that action that he took because in that moment he wasn’t playing. When he’s playing and everybody’s talking about you, it’s easy to do.

“When he was in a difficult moment that time, what he did helped him to after start being in the team and make the impact that he made. I’m very happy with him.”

Tuchel said it was a “close call and a difficult decision” to leave Madueke out of his latest England squad.

Rio Ngumoha, Josh King and Morgan Gibbs-White were among those preferred in forward areas to the 24-year-old.

“That was an option for Thomas,” Arteta said. “There were so many options, he needs to make decisions. He made that one this time. That’s it. I leave it completely to him.”

#1825. Man City XI vs Nottingham Forest: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, injury latest for Premier League

Enzo Maresca is set to keep faith in Gianluigi Donnarumma for Manchester City’s Premier League clash against Nottingham Forest at the weekend.

Donnarumma’s form has been called into question of late and he made another goalkeeping error in the 3-2 win over RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday night, allowing Ridle Baku’s shot to sneak in at his near post.

While Man City’s back-up keeper Geronimo Rulli staked his claim for more game time with an excellent display in the Carabao Cup penalty shootout win over Brighton, it would appear that Donnarumma will remain in between the posts.

Bruno Fernandes is expected to be in the Manchester United starting XI for Sunday's Premier League clash with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

The 32-year-old has scored five goals and registered two assists in 13 appearances for Man United during the 2026-27 campaign.

Fernandes will be bidding to inspire the 20-time English champions to a first Premier League win since the end of August in the team's final game ahead of the November international break.

Here, Sports Mole looks at how Fernandes has performed against Villa during his professional career.

Fernandes has faced Villa on 14 previous occasions in all competitions, boasting a record of 10 wins, two draws and two defeats, scoring seven goals and registering five assists in the process.

In the Premier League, Fernandes has locked horns with Villa on 12 occasions, recording eight wins, in addition to two draws and two defeats, while he has scored six goals and registered four assists against the Lions in England's top flight.

Fernandes has also enjoyed two cup wins over Villa, helping Man United to record a 1-0 victory in the third round of the FA Cup in January 2022, in addition to scoring and providing an assist in a 4-2 success for the Red Devils in the third round of the EFL Cup in November 2022.

The Portugal international actually netted in each of his first three Premier League matches against Villa, while he struck five times in his first five league games against them.

Fernandes has not scored against Villa since hitting the winner in a 1-0 success for Man United at Old Trafford in April 2023.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham are set to remain without Lucas Bergvall for Saturday’s trip to Leeds, but will welcome back Rodrigo Bentancur from suspension.

Bergvall has been out since suffering a knee injury against Manchester United at the start of October, while Bentancur is available after a three-game suspension served following his late dismissal in the same game at Old Trafford.

In the pair’s absence, Roberto De Zerbi has relied on Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes in midfield, and their performances over the last three games have given the Spurs boss plenty to think about with Bentancur coming back into the fold.

Centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo is also back fit after missing the last two games through injury.

De Zerbi confirmed at his pre-match press conference on Friday that Mudryk and fellow winger Savio would not be back until after the international break, though the latter has been seen back with the squad at Hotspur Way this week.

“Savio, Bergvall, Mudryk [are out]. Tosin is available. Yesterday he came inside of the group,” De Zerbi said.

Pedro Porro was named among the substitutes against Palace, but should be fit enough to start at Leeds.

#1820. Crewe Alexandra vs AFC Wimbledon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 06 Nov 2026 09:15, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 15:04

FA Cup first-round action heads to the Mornflake Stadium on Saturday as Crewe Alexandra welcome AFC Wimbledon.

The hosts will be eager to put a recent dip in form behind them, while the visitors arrive looking to end a run of eight games without a competitive victory.

Crewe have made an encouraging start to their League Two campaign, sitting fourth in the table with 22 points to their name.

Although the Railwaymen have not been particularly prolific in front of goal, scoring just 17 times in the league, Lee Bell’s side have proved difficult to beat, suffering only four defeats across all competitions and maintaining an unbeaten record at home.

Unfortunately for the hosts, two of those defeats have come in the last three games, with Crewe enduring a clear dip in form.

A 2-0 defeat away to Exeter City was followed up by a 5-1 thumping at the hands of Chesterfield, before Crewe eventually stopped the slide with a 1-1 home draw against Barnet.

Bell and his men will now turn their attention to the FA Cup, as they look to progress into the second round for the first time since the 2023-24 season.

AFC Wimbledon, meanwhile, will head to the Alexandra Stadium looking to end a miserable run of results across all competitions.

The Dons have lost six of their last seven games, with four of those losses coming in League One - a run which leaves them 18th in the standings.

Johnnie Jackson’s side have only won four games this entire season, and their last success took place all the way back in mid-September, when they edged past Doncaster Rovers 1-0.

More recently, Wimbledon were beaten 2-1 by a strong Stockport County side - a game which saw the Dons surrender a one-goal lead in the final 25 minutes.

Jackson and his men will now turn their attention to FA Cup duties as they prepare to take on a side which they have not faced since February 2025.

Despite this, the Dons will take encouragement from their last head-to-head meeting which saw them secure a comfortable 3-0 victory.

Crewe have added some experience to their midfield options by bringing James Jones back to the club on a short-term contract running until January.

The midfielder previously helped the Railwaymen to promotion back in 2020, and he was most recently playing for Burton Albion.

Jordan Gibson is another midfielder likely to have an important part to play, with the Crewe man having found the net five times in his last seven appearances.

Wimbledon are dealing with injury concerns, most significantly the continued absence of striker Mathew Stevens, who has been sidelined with a hamstring problem since March.

Stevens scored 26 league goals for the Dons over the previous two years, meaning his absence has been a considerable blow, with Harry Cornick and Jayden Stockley shouldering much of the attacking responsibility in recent games.

Fellow forward Dujuan Richards has also been out of action since late September with an injury.

Crewe Alexandra possible starting lineup:

Lawlor; Hutchinson, Stephenson, Offord, Billington; Thomas, Holicek; Gibson, Tabiner, March; McNeill

Bursik; Seddon, Johnson, Yiadom; Sasu, Hippolyte, Harrison, Smith, Tilley; Cornick, Stockley

The visitors may be higher on the football league ladder, but form and momentum cannot be ignored.

Crewe are unbeaten at home this season across all competitions, winning five of their nine games at the Alexandra Stadium, and we’re backing them to extend that run with a narrow victory.

Ryan Gravenberch is Liverpool’s only injury concern ahead of the Premier League clash against Crystal Palace.

The Dutchman, who was dropped for last weekend’s 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal, missed the Champions League loss against Fenerbahce due to a heel injury that prevented him from travelling to Istanbul.

Gravenberch’s availability at the weekend remains up in the air with Andoni Iraola revealing the midfielder is in a race against the clock to prove his fitness ahead of the trip to Selhurst Park.

“The only doubt we will have is Ryan,” the Liverpool head coach said at Friday’s pre-match press conference. “The others will be the same as we have been.

Alisson Becker is under some scrutiny over his performance after the defeat by Fenerbahce, following on from his mistake against Arsenal.

Alexander Isak’s impressive scoring streak may have ended against Arsenal, but the Swede bagged a seventh goal in 13 appearances with his maiden Champions League strike of the season against Fenerbahce.

Isak came off the bench to grab his goal, but he will surely start at the weekend. Bradley Barcola will likely be restored to a more familiar wing role after his experiment up top, with Dutchman Cody Gakpo reintroduced on the other flank.

#1817. Prediction: Inter Milan vs Como

On the back of a derby defeat, wounded Serie A champions Inter Milan will host Como, who have established themselves as regular contenders for European competitions, on Sunday at San Siro.

After 10 rounds in the Italian top flight this season, only two points separate these teams as Inter sit second to Lazio, and Roma wedged in ahead of Como in fourth.

It was a sour blow for the Nerazzurri as they lost to city rivals AC Milan last week, with goals from Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira settling the contest in the first half already, despite Alessandro Bastoni pulling one back. It was the eighth Derby della Madonina in a row which Inter failed to win, and a game which ended a streak of 19 without losing. To be fair to Cristian Chivu, his squad was decimated by illness, and those who played wasted a chance to impress.

Inter bounced back on Tuesday already, beating Feyenoord in the Champions League and showing improvement on what had previously been an underwhelming start in UEFA’s elite competition. Yan Bisseck, Pio Esposito and Piotr Zielinski all found the net in Rotterdam. With half the league phase now played, Chivu’s men sit in 14th place, still in strong contention to qualify for the knockout stage.

History still favours the hosts on Sunday strongly. Inter have won 14 consecutive home games against Como, keeping eight clean sheets in the last nine. It remains to be seen, however, whether that will play any part against Cesc Fabregas’ side this time.

Chivu will be pleased to welcome back a trio of important players in defenders John Stones and Benjamin Pavard, and midfielder Curtis Jones. All three have now returned to full training.

Esposito and Marcus Thuram will most likely be forming the attacking duo, as captain Lautaro Martinez misses out again and is expected back after the upcoming international break. Wing-back Luis Henrique is absent as well.

Since Fabregas took charge of the team in the summer of 2024, Como have been a thoroughly refreshing feature of Italian and European football. Last season they finished fourth and qualified for the Champions League against all odds, and here they are now, fourth again, aiming to do even better this time. Some even see them as genuine title contenders.

After losing away to Feyenoord in mid-October, Como have won six matches in a row in all competitions.

Having triumphed 1-0 at home against Venezia last week, they absolutely annihilated Lens in France on Wednesday, putting nine goals past the Ligue 1 side with seven different goalscorers. Anastasious Douvikas netted a hat-trick, while Nico Paz, Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina, and Matteo Papaccioli, got one each. Ruben Aguilar, who scored the only goal for Lens, cannot be said to have provided any consolation for the hosts.

Therefore, Como will certainly arrive in Milan in good spirits, hoping to finally get this particular scalp. They won’t come to lose, or play merely to avoid defeat.

Como’s recent form is even more impressive given the number of players missing. Forwards Moise Kean, Jayden Addai, Jesus Rodriguez and Assane Diao are all injured, as is defender Trevoh Chalobah.

Nonetheless, Douvikas and Paz are more than capable of causing all sorts of problems for opposition defences, including that of Inter.

For the neutral football lovers, this will surely be a game not to miss, but the supporters of the two sides will need nerves of steel.

Neither defence is likely to withstand the onrush of the opposing attackers, so it wouldn’t be a surprise for the ball to find its way into both nets more than once. As for the outcome, the bookies do favour Inter, but Como will surely have their say on that.

Prediction: Nottingham Forest vs Manchester City

#1816. Atletico Madrid vs. Barcelona: Head-to-head record and past meetings ahead of La Liga clash

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 09:58, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 09:58

One of the biggest matches on the Spanish football calendar will take place in Madrid on Sunday evening, as Atletico Madrid welcome Barcelona.

The hosts are second in the La Liga table, boasting a record of nine wins, one draw and one defeat from their opening 11 matches of the campaign.

Meanwhile, Barcelona are at the summit, with their record this season standing at 10 wins and one defeat from 11 fixtures.

Barcelona are two points clear of second-placed Atletico, while third-placed Real Madrid are only three points off the top at this stage of proceedings.

Atletico will enter this match off the back of a 2-0 home defeat to Bayern Munich in the Champions League, while Barcelona recorded a 3-0 victory over Aston Villa last time out in the same competition.

Here, Sports Mole looks at the head-to-head record and past meetings between the two teams ahead of their contest in the Spanish capital.

Barcelona lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having recorded 116 wins to Atletico's 80, while there have also been 57 draws in this particular fixture.

The Catalan outfit have also comfortably outscored their opponents, finding the back of the net on 475 occasions in their 252 matches against Atletico, while the capital outfit have managed 367.

Lionel Messi is the leading goalscorer in this fixture, finding the back of the net on 32 occasions against Atletico, which is 16 ahead of Cesar Rodriguez in second position.

Unsurprisingly, Barcelona also lead the head-to-head record in La Liga, winning 83 of their 178 matches to Atletico's 53, while there have also been 42 draws in Spain's top flight.

Thirteen of the last 19 meetings between these two sides have come in La Liga, and Barcelona had been on a five-game winning run against Atletico at that level, including 1-0 and 3-0 successes during the 2023-24 campaign.

However, Atletico shocked their rivals in December 2024 with a 2-1 victory at Estadi Olimpic Lluis Companys, with Alexander Sorloth netting a last-gasp winner.

Barcelona did manage to gain revenge in the reverse match at Wanda Metropolitano, coming from two goals behind late on to record a 4-2 victory against their title rivals, and Blaugrana made it back-to-back wins in this fixture with a 3-1 triumph in December 2025.

The pair have also met in the semi-finals of the Copa del Rey in 2025-26, with Atletico running out 4-3 winners on aggregate, but Barcelona won their last league match 2-1 in April 2026, with Robert Lewandowski netting a late winner to send Hansi Flick's side seven points clear at the top of La Liga.

In the Champions League, the pair have met six times, with Atletico recording three wins and suffering two defeats, and their three previous quarter-final ties in the competition have ended in Atletico advancing to the semi-finals.

Most recently, in the 2025-26 quarter-finals, Atletico Madrid sealed a 2-0 first leg victory away from home before narrowly losing 2-1 in the reverse fixture, meaning Simeone's side still managed to advance as 3-2 winners on aggregate.

#1815. Arsenal XI vs Hull: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, injury latest for Premier League

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

William Saliba is in contention to get his first minutes of the season when Arsenal host Hull in the Premier League on Saturday.

The Frenchman has missed the entirety of the campaign so far with a long-term back injury exacerbated at the World Cup but is now closing in on a return to competitive action.

Saliba was an unused substitute against Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday night and is expected to make Mikel Arteta’s matchday squad again this weekend.

While Arsenal will be cautious with his fitness and it would be a surprise if Saliba came straight in to start against Hull, he could well feature off the bench if the game state allows.

There was some concern over Ezri Konsa’s fitness after he had to come off in Prague following a knee problem, but that is not a serious issue and he is available to face Hull.

“Yeah, he’s fine,” Arteta said at his pre-match press conference on Friday. “He was feeling much better today. We took him out for a precaution but yesterday and today he’s feeling good.”

Riccardo Calafiori was given a full rest for Arsenal’s 2-1 win over Slavia and should come back into the side here.

Bruno Guimaraes also did not feature at all in the Czech Republic and looks the obvious choice to partner Declan Rice in midfield.

In the absence of the injured Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke continues to impress and he is effectively the only option on the right wing with Max Dowman suspended for the next two Premier League matches.

There is a tougher call for Arteta to make on the left wing. Christos Tzolis was sharp on his return from injury last weekend against Liverpool at Anfield, but Eberechi Eze produced a strong display against Slavia to push his case.

Kai Havertz will hope to come back in to lead the line, even though Viktor Gyokeres produced a goal and an assist last time out.

#1813. Arsenal handed new William Saliba boost after France squad announcement

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal have been handed a welcome boost over William Saliba after Zinedine Zidane named his second France squad.

Former Real Madrid head coach Zidane is preparing to take charge of Les Bleus for just the fifth time after replacing Didier Deschamps, who stood down following the 2026 World Cup in north America earlier this summer.

The first post-World Cup international window was an extended one which lasted three weeks with France facing Belgium twice, Italy and Turkey in a Nations League quadruple-header.

France took four points from a possible 12 to sit top of League A, Group 1 ahead of facing Italy and Turkey within the next nine days.

Zidane’s first France squad did not contain Saliba as the Arsenal defender was still recovering from a back injury sustained while playing for the national team in the World Cup semi-final against eventual winners Spain.

Saliba has since resumed full fitness. He played 45 minutes for the Gunners in a behind-closed-doors friendly last week before travelling with the squad to the Czech Republic for the 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

However, the 25-year-old has not been selected by Zidane for France duty this month.

The news will be welcomed by Mikel Arteta as Saliba should benefit from more time in training, though the Frenchman will miss out on some valuable minutes to build up his match sharpness.

“We’ve been in very close contact,” Arteta said on Friday ahead of Arsenal’s Premier League clash against Hull. “They’re announcing [their squad] at 5pm this evening.

“They have all the information, now it’s about them, about Zinedine in this case to make the call. We will accept whatever it is.”

After the international break, Arsenal face Newcastle at St James’ Park, with home games to follow against Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City.

#1811. England squad confirmed as Cole Palmer, Ben White, Josh King decisions revealed

By Ben Knapton | 06 Nov 2026 10:01, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 10:14

England manager Thomas Tuchel has announced his Three Lions squad for November's UEFA Nations League games against Spain and Croatia.

Tuchel's side sit on nine points from their opening three matches in League A Group 3, six clear of third-placed Croatia, meaning they only need one draw from their final two games to advance to the quarter-finals.

England host Croatia at Wembley next Thursday evening in their penultimate group game, three days before closing out the opening round away to Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium.

All eyes would have been on whether Chelsea's Cole Palmer would return to the squad, having been criticised by Tuchel after withdrawing from the September/October selection through injury.

Even though Palmer is fully fit and available, the 24-year-old has been snubbed by Tuchel, who has instead handed senior call-ups to Josh King and Jobe Bellingham.

Fulham starlet King was part of England's pre-World Cup squad over the summer, and the 19-year-old has been rewarded for registering two goals and one assist in his first nine Premier League games of the season.

Meanwhile, Borussia Dortmund 21-year-old Bellingham - who links up with older brother Jude Bellingham - has been promoted from the Under-21s after setting up three goals in 14 games so far in 2026-27.

Jobe Bellingham and King are also preferred to Manchester City's Phil Foden, and there is also no place in the midfield ranks for Kobbie Mainoo or Jordan Henderson.

Elsewhere, Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane will break Peter Shilton's all-time caps record of 125 if he plays just one second of the November break, and Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin has been nominated as his backup once again.

Arsenal's Eberechi Eze, Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha and Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White line up in attack too, but Marcus Rashford - recovering from a hip injury - and Noni Madueke miss out.

Further back, Arsenal defender Ben White is in the squad for the first time since March, having missed both the World Cup and the September/October selection due to injury.

White replaces the injured Trevoh Chalobah, and there is also a recall for Inter Milan's Djed Spence, another defender who was unavailable at the start of the Nations League campaign.

White's Arsenal teammate Ezri Konsa has been nominated too, suggesting that the injury he sustained in the Gunners' Champions League victory over Slavia Prague in midweek is not serious.

However, Crystal Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson has been left out despite recovering from his own fitness problem, as Jason Steele joins James Trafford and Jordan Pickford once again.

#1810. Arsenal sensation Max Dowman handed major new boost despite two red cards

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal youngster Max Dowman has been handed his maiden call-up to the England Under-21s squad.

The Gunners sensation, 16, was on Friday named in head coach Lee Carsley’s 23-man Young Lions group for upcoming friendlies against Portugal and France.

It is the first time that Dowman will step up to U21 football at international level, having previously represented his country in the U16, U17 and U19 age categories.

He was sent off on his last appearance for the U19s in a behind-closed-doors friendly against the United States last month.

Dowman was then dismissed late on while playing for Arsenal in their shock Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood for retaliating following a heavy challenge, with the Gunners’ appeal against his ban rejected by the Football Association (FA).

That drew a visibly furious reaction from manager Mikel Arteta, who had some choice words for the teenager as he trudged off having spoken to him before the match about not reacting to any rough treatment.

Arteta was criticised in some quarters for his response to Dowman’s red card at Fleetwood, but later doubled down on his approach and insisted “we are not in Disneyland” as he warned that the player had to meet the same standards as the rest of the first-team squad.

Dowman is joined in England’s U21s squad by Arsenal team-mates Tommy Setford and Ethan Nwaneri, currently out on loan at Stevenage and Borussia Dortmund respectively, plus former Gunners youngsters Brooke Norton-Cuffy and Amario Cozier-Duberry.

Other standout selections include soaring Liverpool midfielder Trey Nyoni, plus Tottenham star Archie Gray, Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong and Manchester City full-back Rico Lewis, who was drafted into the senior squad last month following the injury to club team-mate Nico O’Reilly.

However, Liverpool teenager Rio Ngumoha has been promoted to the senior squad by Thomas Tuchel, while prolific Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear misses out through injury.

Following a goalless home draw with Slovakia, Carsley’s side last month qualified for the 2027 U21 European Championship, which takes place in Albania and Serbia next summer.

Their unbeaten run in qualifying was only ended by defeat to the Republic of Ireland in the final fixture, with England the current reigning back-to-back U21 champions of Europe after winning titles in both 2023 and 2025.

#1809. Mourinho says Madrid need to start games stronger ahead of Valencia trip

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jose Mourinho knows Real Madrid must be more consistent at the start of games, saying their recent history of comebacks is both a positive and a negative.

Madrid visit Valencia in LaLiga this Saturday, and a head-to-head meeting between Atletico Madrid and Barcelona the following day means they have a chance to make up ground at the top of the table.

Los Blancos sit third after 11 games, one point below cross-city rivals Atleti and three adrift of Barca, who lead the way.

Mourinho's side thrashed Racing Santander 3-0 in their most recent league game, but they had a much tougher test in the Champions League on Wednesday, twice falling behind to AEK Athens before recovering for a 3-2 victory.

"It's better not to have to come from behind, it's better to have things like in Santander, where it was 3-0 and could have been four or five by half-time," Mourinho told reporters on Friday.

"Coming from behind means many positive things, but also some negatives. The positives are the belief in the group, the friendship, that openness to risky situations, a strong bench, group motivation and knowing what jersey you are wearing…

"But it also has a negative side, and we need to work on it, finding more consistency in starting games well, like in Santander. There's a lot for us to do."

Our squad for the match!  @ValenciaCF_en https://t.co/lmKpSryRs0

— Real Madrid C.F.  (@realmadriden) November 6, 2026

Saturday's game will be the last one where Madrid are without Vinicius Junior, after he was suspended for four games after being sent off for pulling Nathan Saliba's hair during a win over Villarreal last month.

But Mourinho says it may not be as simple as Vinicius walking back into their starting line-up after the international break.

"For me, the most important thing is the team. I would never harm the team to benefit a player. When we return to normal with Vini being available, I will manage it," he said.

"I want the team to think game by game, but as a coach, I have to think about the next few matches and the sequence of games we have.

"The most straightforward answer to your question is that a coach must do everything to have his players at the highest level.

"We always expect the Vini who eliminated me from the Champions League with Benfica, and that version exists.

"We must continue exploring all strategies at all levels. When deciding who plays, the team is always above the individual."

Valencia are 19th in the table ahead of this weekend's fixtures, having beaten Elche 1-0 last time out to earn their first victory under former Mexico boss Javier Aguirre.

Michael Carrick has said that it is “possible” for Manchester United to get back to the glory years of Sir Alex Ferguson’s tenure.

The former midfielder solidified himself as a club legend under the Scot during his playing career at Old Trafford, and now he sits in the same hotseat that Ferguson left in 2013.

Carrick, meanwhile, is under serious pressure after just one win in 10 games leaves United 17th in the Premier League table, although the winless run was snapped on Tuesday with a dramatic 3-2 victory over Roma in the Champions League.

The Red Devils have endured their worst start to a campaign in 40 years, and comparisons have been made between Carrick’s opening games of his first season in charge to Ferguson’s in 1990.

Ferguson, who was appointed United boss in 1986, was spared what had seemed to be an inevitable sacking after he beat Nottingham Forest in the FA Cup in January 1990 after a woeful start to the season that saw his side 15th in the table, with results including a 5-1 hammering by Manchester City.

Carrick has suffered the same fate this term, with many believing that he would be dismissed after the 4-1 and 3-0 defeats by Como and Bourenmouth a fortnight ago.

He was retained in-post by the club’s hierarchy ahead of the 2-0 loss at Chelsea, with it believed that the club’s hierarchy want to reassess his position during the November international break.

Ahead of another crucial Premier League tie, this time against Aston Villa, Carrick looked positively at what the future could hold for his side.

"It's difficult to bring success. It was difficult then, and it's difficult now," he said.

"It just shows you how tough it is to have sustained success, never mind moments of success.

"We've got to live in the moment. We know what we've got to do, and we've got to be focused on bringing success week to week in games.

"Then things fall into place. If you do that enough, and do it often enough, you'll bring a bigger version of it.”

The ex-England international was asked whether his current United team could be held to the same standards as that of Ferguson’s pomp, to which the head coach replied: "It's not impossible. Anything's possible.

"You've got to build. You've got to be realistic, and you've got to put things into perspective as well.

"Look at the recent history we've had, where we're trying to get to and what we want to achieve. It's not going to happen in a blink of an eye. It's not going to happen overnight.

"Success does take time, and we don't like having to spend time, but it does take a period of time to build.

"We showed a really quick response and improved a lot last season, and that shows what's possible.

"The game has certainly changed, no doubt. It always does. It evolves, and it had evolved by the time Sir Alex came in, probably after Sir Matt and the years following that.

"It evolves all the time. That's how it is. It changes, and we've got to deal with what's in front of us. That's us.

"I understand the comparisons. There's always different things to compare, but we have to live in the present as well and definitely use past experiences to help us.

"Time and patience, but we're all desperate to win football matches and win them as quickly as we possibly can."

On Thursday evening, Ferencvaros will travel to San Siro to face AC Milan in the Europa League, in a must-win game for the Rossoneri.

➤ Manager: Balazs Borbely ➤ Form (all comps): D-W-W-W-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Europa League): Kristoffer Zachariassen – 5 ➤ Most assists (Europa League): Yusuf Bamidele & Veljko Birmančević – 2 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bero, Otvos.

Ferencvaros went into last season as defending league champions under head coach Robbie Keane, but were forced to settle for second place. They did win the domestic cup though, and got to the last-16 of the Europa League before being beaten by Braga.

Keane left before the 2026-27 campaign, and he was replaced by Balazs Borbely who came from Gyor ETO, the club that have been one of the surprise packages in recent years, even winning the Nemzeti Bajnokság I (league title) last season.

It was quite a quiet summer for the Budapest-based team, as their big splash was Veljko Birmancevic from Sparta Praha for €2m. Matus Bero and Nathan Zohore arrived on free transfers, while Adam Nagy joined for a low fee from Spezia.

There were a few more exits though: Elton Acolatse, Zsombor Gruber, Mohammed Abu Fani, Gabi Kanichowsky and Cebrail Makreckis all left for figures between €2.5m and €1m, while five departed on free transfers too.

It has been a good start for Borbely, given that Ferencvaros are undefeated in their last 20 matches across all competitions, and they are dreaming of securing direct qualification to the last-16 of the competition.

The Zöldek have three wins from three, occupying fourth place in the overall standings behind Benfica, Bayer Leverkusen and Bournemouth. To qualify for the group stage, they overcame Twente, Gornik Zabrze and Trabzonspor, beating the latter 5-0 on aggregate.

An away win against Celtic kicked off their league phase, following by victories against Viktoria Plzen and Torreense. Overall, the Hungarian outfit have scored nine times and have conceded just three in what has been a perfect start in the UEL.

Ferencvaros’ only defeat came in their league debut on July 26 (2-4 against Baksi FC). Since then, they have gone on a long unbeaten streak of five wins and five draws, climbing to third place, just two points behind league leaders Gyor and with a game in hand.

In terms of injury news, the visitors will be missing Slovakian midfielder Matus Bero, while Bence Otvos is recovering from an ACL injury and will not take part. Aside from that, they have a clean bill of health.

Borbely’s side have so far alternated between a 4-1-4-1 formation – deploying former Liverpool player Nabi Keita or Adamy Nagy (who played for Bologna and Spezia) as midfielders – and a 4-2-3-1 to offer a bit more width.

A few rotations are expected from the weekend’s game – where they cruised to a 2-0 win – and the first set comes in defence. Radnoti, Nagy, Zohore and O’Dowda are all expected to return to the starting XI, with Gomez being the only survivor to retain his place.

Maiga will find a new partner at the base of the midfield in the aforementioned Nagy, whilst Zachariassen will start ahead of them.

On the wings, it’s an unchanged set-up with leading goalscorer Zachariassen and Birmancevic starting. Then, Yusuf is expected to return to the starting XI.

Predicted Ferencvaros XI (4-2-3-1): Radnoti; O. Nagy, Zohore, Gomez, O’Dowda; Maiga, A. Nagy; Arzani, Zachariassen, Birmancevic; Yusuf.

Predicted bench: A Varga, Dibusz, Osvath, Raemaekers, Cadu, Madrasz, Corbu, Bamidele, Bero, Joseph, Levi, Arzani, Rommens, Pappoe, Z Varga, Keita.

#1806. Ex-Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United star Sebastien Bassong is fined for dodging £7 Tube fare by using someone else's travelcard

Published: 13:02 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 16:13 EDT, 2 November 2026

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Sebastien Bassong has been fined for dodging a £7 Tube fare after he was caught using someone else's train driver pass illegally.

The Frenchman, 40, who spent several seasons in the Premier League with Spurs, Newcastle and Norwich, was stopped by a Transport for London (TfL) officer after he was spotted tailgating a friend through the barriers at St Paul's station in May.

The ex-footballer was carrying the Oystercard of the friend's ex-girlfriend, which had been issued to her as a driver on the Docklands Light Railway (DLR), court documents showed.

The TfL officer was then told that Bassong, who was an £8 million signing for Spurs in 2009, had been using her travelcard because he was 'experiencing financial and personal hardship due to a divorce and unemployment'.

Bassong was convicted of using the rail network without a valid ticket at Wimbledon Magistrates Court on October 30.

Magistrate Graham Burbage fined him £220, ordered him to pay the £7 fare for his journey from Arnos Grove to St Paul's, and directed him to pay £250 in prosecution costs and an £88 victim surcharge.

Bassong did not enter a plea to the charge, and was convicted behind closed doors in a Single Justice Procedure hearing.

Adebukola Anifowose, a revenue control officer for TfL, told the court in a statement she spotted Bassong at 1.08pm 'pretend to tap an Oystercard enclosed in a white wallet before tailgating through the wide-aisle gate behind another male'.

Sebastien Bassong in action during a Premier League match between Chelsea and Tottenham at Stamford Bridge in 2009

Bassong attended the 2026 PFA Awards at the Manchester Opera House

The star playing for Spurs during the UEFA Champions League  match between BSC Young Boys and Tottenham Hotspur in 2010

She said Bassong offered up a TfL staff nominee pass when challenged, which allows free travel on London transport.

'System checks later confirmed that the pass did not belong to him and had last been used in October 2025,' she said.

'The accompanying male was spoken to – this individual later informed me that he was assisting Mr Bassong, who was experiencing financial and personal hardship due to a divorce and unemployment, by providing him with the nominee pass.

'It was subsequently established that the pass was registered to an ex-girlfriend of this male, who reportedly claimed to be a DLR driver.'

A notice about the prosecution was sent to Bassong's north London home, and he did not respond before the court hearing.

Bassong, who now runs a motivational coaching business, has been given 28 days to settle the court bill totalling £565.

#1805. Atletico Madrid vs Barcelona - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 10:46, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 20:31

One of the biggest matches on the Spanish football calendar will take place at the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday night, as Atletico Madrid host Barcelona in La Liga.

It is a meeting between the top two in the La Liga table, with Barca currently at the summit on 30 points, while Atletico are second on 28 points.

Atletico have not won the La Liga title since 2020-21, and they finished fourth in Spain's top flight last season, 25 points off the champions Barcelona, but this Atleti team have the look of a side capable of making a strong challenge for the trophy in 2026-27.

Diego Simeone's team have won nine, drawn one and lost one of their 11 league matches, while boasting the best defensive record with just eight goals conceded.

Atletico have won each of their last seven league matches, including a 2-1 success over Real Madrid before the last international break, and they will now be bidding to enter the upcoming international period off the back of a victory over the champions.

The Red and Whites posted a 2-0 victory over Levante in their last league match, but they will enter this fixture off the back of a defeat, going down 2-0 at home to Bayern Munich in the league stage of the Champions League on Tuesday night.

Atletico knocked Barcelona out in the quarter-finals of last season's Champions League, but they have not overcome the Catalan team in the league since December 2024.

Barcelona are actually unbeaten away from home against Atletico in the league since October 2021, so they will be protecting a strong record in this match.

Hansi Flick's side saw an 11-game winning run at the start of the campaign come to an end on October 20, when they were beaten 4-2 by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League, before losing 2-1 at home to Real Madrid in La Liga five days later.

However, the Catalan team have managed to win their last two matches, posting a 6-1 victory over Alaves in the league last time out, before beating Aston Villa 3-0 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

Barcelona are top of the La Liga table on 30 points and have incredibly scored 46 times in their 11 domestic matches, which is more than double Atletico's goal tally (22).

Flick's team are once again title favourites, but the recent defeat to Real Madrid was a real setback, and it is shaping up to be another fascinating contest in the Spanish capital on Sunday, as second welcomes first.

Atletico will be without the services of Cristian Romero (muscle) and Johnny Cardoso (thigh), but Morten Hjulmand will return to the squad, having missed the Champions League contest with Bayern last time out through injury.

Lee Kang-in is expected to be introduced back into the starting side on Sunday, with the 25-year-old potentially featuring alongside Julian Alvarez in the final third of the field.

Alvarez is set to line up against the team that he wanted to join over the summer, and the Argentina international will be bidding to add to the one league goal that he has scored during the 2026-27 campaign.

As for Barcelona, Dani Olmo (adductor), Roony Bardghji (knee) and Xavi Espart (ankle) are definitely out of the match, while Eric Garcia (thigh), Jules Kounde (ankle) and Andreas Christensen (thigh) all face late assessments.

Rodri (hamstring) was forced off against Aston Villa last time out and will also be absent, which could open the door for Marc Bernal to feature alongside Pedri in midfield.

Brian Farinas should retain his spot at right-back for Barcelona, while Anthony Gordon is expected to be selected alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha in the final third of the field.

Atletico Madrid possible starting lineup:

Oblak; Llorente, Pubill, Hancko, Grimaldo; Simeone, Barrios, Hjulmand, Baena; Lee, Alvarez

J Garcia; Farinas, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Bernal, Pedri; Yamal, Fermin, Gordon; Raphinha

This is such a difficult match to call; we came close to backing a draw - either 1-1 or 2-2 - but have ultimately settled on a narrow success for the reigning champions.

#1804. Michael Carrick replacement race takes another twist as key Manchester United figure 'set for exit'

Manchester United could lose a key member of staff who will have a big say in who replaces Michael Carrick, should the current head coach be sacked.

Carrick has come under immense scrutiny after a run of just one win in 10 games across all competitions, with that streak stretching back to late August.

The Red Devils snapped that nine-game stretch without a victory on Tuesday in a dramatic 3-2 comeback against Roma in the Champions League, which could well have saved their under-fire boss.

Many thought that Carrick would be dismissed a fortnight ago after heavy defeats by Como and Bournemouth - 4-1 and 3-0 respectively - but he was kept on for the trip to Chelsea, which United lost 2-0, as Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer netted while Lisandro Martinez was sent off.

It appears that the head coach will be given until the November international break, when it has been reported that the club’s hierarchy will reassess his position, following the home Premier League game against Aston Villa on Sunday.

It is believed that there are three potential replacements that United are targeting should they decide to make a change in the dugout, with Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler all under consideration.

Nagelsmann, the former Bayern Munich and Germany boss, has an internal ally which could hand him an advantage in the race to replace Carrick.

That is Christopher Vivell, United’s director of recruitment, who the German worked with at RB Leipzig.

However, a spanner could be thrown in the works, with German outlet Bild claiming that Bayern Munich are interested in appointing Vivell.

It comes after the Bundesliga champions terminated their head of scouting Nils Schmadtke’s contract three days ago, and they have identified Vivell as an ideal replacement.

Should Vivell, who also worked for a short period at Chelsea, move back to Germany, that could come as a serious blow to Nagelsmann’s chances of landing the job at Old Trafford.

#1802. ​Olsen not viewing Decision Day as a playoff rehearsal for Houston Dynamo

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Ben Olsen will not treat the Houston Dynamo's Decision Day matchup with St. Louis City SC like a playoff game, though he still expects his players to give everything as the sides jostle for position ahead of the postseason.

The Dynamo sit fifth in the Western Conference with one regular-season game remaining, level on points with fourth-placed St. Louis.

Both teams are assured of their MLS Cup Playoff places, but with the San Jose Earthquakes only a point better off than the duo in third, they have a chance to improve their respective seedings going into the postseason.

Houston were in good form before losing 3-1 to the Portland Timbers on Sunday, and though Olsen wants a response this weekend, he is not placing too much importance on the game.

"It's not a playoff game. When it's a playoff game, it will be a playoff game. When it's the last day of the season, it'll just be the last day of the season," Olsen told reporters.

"We're going to go after it – we'll put our group together and prepare to give everything we have."

Asked where he felt Houston came up short against Portland, Olsen added: "The standings don't mean anything in this league – they never have and they never will.

"As long as the league continues with this format, in this way, that will be the case. This [Portland] was not a team that we took lightly – they're a good team.

"I just didn't think we were sharp enough in some of those moments. That can come down to a bunch of different things; it can be fatigue, it can just be quality, and I think we were just second-best there."

#1799. Footy Headlines: ‘An unexpected blend’ – Puma to end Milan kit run with ‘streetwear’ third shirt

Today, some news has emerged about AC Milan’s possible new third shirt for the 2027-28 season and the colours it’ll be.

The big kit news today has been the move to Adidas and how much Milan will pocket from it. After signing with Puma on a deal worth €16 million per season, they renewed on a €30m per season deal for the ‘second half’ of their relationship.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, Adidas will now blow this figure out of the park, with a €500m agreement over a 10-year period. A substantial increase, especially when paired with the stadium figures.

According to Footy Headlines, the third kit will feature an ‘unexpected blend’ of colours, with a ‘Dark Umber’ and ‘Court Grey’ design. The former is an almost-black, brownish colour, whilst the latter is a ‘mid-tone’.

To contrast this, the detailing on the shirt will be ‘vibrantly’ red, to ensure it still stands out. A kit with another ‘streetwear’-y feel to it, it will try to merge with a sophisticated look, too.

Of course, this will also be the final ‘traditional’ kit produced by the brand – in terms of a home, away and alternative shirt – and it almost reflects the end of the partnership. Based on the initial leaks of the home and away shirts, it seems like a nice mix of shirts to see off the brand’s relationship.

#1798. Manchester United handed major transfer boost as key target 'up for sale'

Manchester United have been bolstered in their pursuit of a left-back.

The Red Devils have been hamstrung in that position this term, with natural options Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu both struck down with injuries that have kept them out for long spells.

As such, it has forced under-fire manager Michael Carrick to experiment with makeshift solutions in the interim, with right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui both depuitising there, while central defender Ayden Heaven has also been shifted out wide to cover with limited success.

As such, it makes the role a key position that needs strengthening at Old Trafford, with many United fans believing that a left-back should have been signed in the summer.

Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall was thought to be the priority target, but Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde was also a reported option.

Should United reignite their interest in the Spaniard, they could well find a deal with their Catalan rivals relatively easy to come by.

That is because The Athletic reports that Hansi Flick’s side want to sell Balde, a stance they have held since the summer transfer window.

They could not sanction a sale of the defender, who was keen to try and play his way back into his manager’s plans despite being told that he was surplus to requirements.

Barcelona’s cash-strapped situtation - as well as their need to raise funds to sign a new left-sided centre-back - will also make them more desperate to sell Balde.

Despite the 23-year-old’s willingness to stay at his boyhood club, he has been limited to just 124 minutes this term.

With Shaw’s contract up at the end of the season and Dorgu not a true left-back under current boss Carrick, a deal for Balde could well prove an enticing, cut-price option for the Red Devils.

Manchester United have been bolstered in their pursuit of a left-back.

#1796. Estoril Praia vs Maritimo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 06 Nov 2026 11:08, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 11:09

Estoril Praia play host to Maritimo on Sunday still searching for their first Portuguese top-flight win of the season.

At a time when the home side sit bottom of the Primeira Liga table, Maritimo are six points ahead of them in 14th place.

Although Estoril finished in 10th position last season, it masked over the issues that the team were suffering from at the end of last season.

Collecting just two points from their closing eight games of 2025-26 has been followed by accumulating the same amount of points in their opening 10 fixtures of 2026-27.

A combined total of four points from 18 encounters has led to several managerial changes, with Leandro Pires the current caretaker incumbent.

Under-23 boss Sergio Raimundo took charge of the last match, a trip to Porto that ended in a routine 4-0 win for the league leaders.

As well as remaining with just five goals to their name this season, Estoril have conceded 12 times across five consecutive defeats.

Meanwhile, Maritimo have posted three defeats in a row, losing to Porto, Vitoria de Guimaraes and Santa Clara respectively.

While they remain six points above bottom, Mitchell van der Gaag's side are just one point ahead of 17th spot.

Given their newly-promoted status, they will remain satisfied with their current plight, but they possess the worst away defensive record in the division with 12 goals conceded in five fixtures.

That said, some positives may be taken from only losing 2-1 at Sporting Lisbon in the Taca de Liga, before succumbing 2-0 to fourth-placed Santa Clara last time out.

Pires is expected to make a number of alterations to the Estoril XI, with Jordan Holsgrove among the players expected to be recalled.

Axel Camblan and Xeka may also be provided with opportunities, depending on how many alterations are made in midfield.

Ricard Sanchez can also expect to return at right-back or right-midfield as Pires looks to stumble upon a winning formula.

Meanwhile, Simo Bouzaidi could return to the Maritimo attack, potentially in place of Mons Bassouamina who he replaced in the previous fixture.

With Maritimo having giving a solid account of themselves against Santa Clara, Van der Gaag may be against making other changes.

Vladan Danilovic, Yellu Santiago and Maxime Dominguez are all expected to remain sidelined.

Turk; Carvalho, Andreou, Ferro, Parente; Sanchez, Tsoungui, Holsgrove, Xeka, Peixinho; Lacximicant

With both clubs on such poor runs of form in the Primeira Liga, this is a difficult match to call. However, based on their superior goals record during the early phase of the top-flight campaign, we are backing the visitors to come through in a tense contest.
